name: – Jaroslav Bžoch – Draft Council decision
title: RECOMMENDATION on the draft Council decision on the conclusion on behalf of the European Union of the Agreement between the European Union and the Republic of Lebanon on the cooperation between the European Union Agency for Criminal Justice Cooperation (Eurojust) and the authorities of the Republic of Lebanon competent for judicial cooperation in criminal matters
part_text:
The European Parliament agrees to a deal between the European Union and Lebanon on fighting serious crime together. The deal lets Eurojust, the European Union's agency for criminal justice cooperation, share information with Lebanese judicial authorities. Lebanon will send a prosecutor to work at Eurojust alongside prosecutors from European Union countries. The report says the deal includes strong rules to protect people's personal data and rights. Parliament's role here is only to say yes or no to the deal, and it says yes.

- **What changes:** Eurojust and Lebanese authorities can exchange information on serious cross-border crimes, with data protection safeguards.
- **Who it affects:** Prosecutors in European Union countries and Lebanon working on cases like terrorism, cybercrime and drug trafficking.
- **What happens next:** Parliament has given its consent, so the deal can now be formally concluded and take effect.
